## Detailed entries

### City of Chesapeake

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** 2026-07-21 (City Council adopted Resolution 26-R-042 by a 9-0 vote)
- **Date field:** `2026-07-21` (exact)
- **Duration:** 8 months from adoption, or until City Council takes final action on comprehensive plan amendment PLN-COMP-2026-002, whichever occurs first
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `va-city-of-chesapeake-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Resolution 26-R-042, adopted by Chesapeake City Council 9-0 on July 21, 2026
- **What prompted it:** Council sought to pause discretionary review of data center land-use applications while comprehensive plan amendment PLN-COMP-2026-002 is pending
- **Affected projects:** No single named project; applies citywide to discretionary data center land-use applications pending before the Planning Commission or City Council.
- **Status notes:** Active as of 2026-09-23. The Resolution 26-R-042 deferral remains in force, running 8 months from its July 21, 2026 adoption (to approximately 2027-03-21) or until Council takes final action on comprehensive plan amendment PLN-COMP-2026-002, whichever occurs first. On August 18, 2026 the City Council separately and unanimously adopted a zoning ordinance amendment that requires a conditional use permit for data centers across the city except within Coastal Virginia Commerce Park (CoVAC), where the city says data centers may still be built by-right, and prohibits data centers from drawing groundwater; this closed a loophole that could have let a data center proceed administratively despite the moratorium, but it is a permanent zoning change layered on top of, not a replacement for, the still-active Resolution 26-R-042 deferral. The zoning change was prompted partly by Praetorian Fund's August 2026 purchase of the Frank Williams Farm Tract (Coastal Virginia Commerce Park); because that site does not connect to public utilities, city officials confirmed the moratorium independently applies to it. No repeal, extension, or expiration of the moratorium itself was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
- **Outcome:** Enacted deferral of discretionary data center land-use applications pending completion of a related comprehensive plan amendment.

### Fluvanna County

- **Affected projects:** No named project or MW total identified in the captured packets; contemporaneous rezoning comments raised concern about possible data center use.

A separate August 2026 report describes a later pause through December 31 while a further zoning change was considered; it is a distinct action.
- **Outcome:** ZTA 25:10 moved data centers from by-right use to special use permit treatment in I-1 and I-2 and modified the data center definition.

### Front Royal

- **Type:** Town
- **Status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Recorded date:** 2026-07-06, Front Royal Town Council work session, 6-0 vote (Vice Mayor Amber F. Veitenthal and Councilmembers DeDomenico-Payne, Ingram, Rappaport, Sealock, and Wood; Mayor Cockrell present but votes only to break ties), per the town's own approved council minutes.
- **Date field:** `2026-07-06` (exact)
- **Duration:** 90-day administrative moratorium adopted 2026-07-06; council extended it by an additional 60 days on 2026-09-28. The exact final end date and effect of the later zoning action remain unverified.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `va-front-royal-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Resolution Establishing a Temporary Ninety (90) Day Moratorium on the Acceptance of Data Center Land Use Applications, adopted 6-0 by Front Royal Town Council at its July 6, 2026 work session. Town Attorney George Sonnett advised the moratorium was structured as an administrative action (rather than a legislative zoning-ordinance amendment) because, in his opinion, Virginia law does not authorize a legislative moratorium through the zoning ordinance.
- **What prompted it:** The town sought to preserve the status quo while it drafts a permanent zoning text amendment to define data centers separately from 'technology' uses and prohibit data centers in all town zoning districts; no data center application had been received as of adoption.
- **Affected projects:** None named; Town Manager Joseph Petty confirmed no data center applications had been received as of the July 6, 2026 vote.
- **Status notes:** The 90-day application moratorium adopted 2026-07-06 was extended by 60 days on 2026-09-28. Local news reports the council unanimously adopted a zoning text prohibition on 2026-10-26, after the September work-session review. Whether that action terminated the administrative moratorium and its exact end date remain unresolved.
- **Outcome:** Front Royal Town Council adopted a 90-day administrative moratorium on data center land-use applications while it drafts a permanent zoning prohibition.

### Loudoun County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** 2026-09-15, Loudoun County Board of Supervisors vote, as reported in its September 16 release; the base pause and grid-reliability exception each passed 7-1-1.
- **Date field:** `2026-09-15` (exact)
- **Duration:** The September 15 immediate pause was tied to Phase 2 of the Data Center Standards and Locations initiative. A formal resolution proposed a limit of 12 months from each application’s first submission to the Planning Commission; its October 20 consideration was deferred to November 17.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `va-loudoun-county-2026`
- **Authority and source:** September 15, 2026 Board action, described in the county’s September 16 release as an immediate pause on consideration of certain legislative applications with a grid-reliability exception. The October 20 proposed formal resolution was deferred; its proposed per-application limit and retroactive language are not treated as adopted. Grandfathered administrative cases were reported unaffected. The prior record attributes to the County Attorney that Virginia law does not permit a blanket moratorium on administrative applications and reports roughly 17 grandfathered cases totaling more than 11 million square feet under the March 2025 resolution.
- **What prompted it:** Regulatory gap and community pressure over rapid data center growth in the county ("Data Center Alley"); effort led by Algonkian District Supervisor Juli Briskman, tied to the county's ongoing Phase 2 Data Center Standards and Locations initiative (begun September 2025) addressing data center/substation siting, noise, building heights, on-site power generation, and battery storage standards.
- **Affected projects:** At least 17 land-use cases representing more than 11 million square feet of data center development are 'grandfathered' under the county's March 2025 resolution and continue through by-right administrative review, unaffected by this pause.
- **Status notes:** The county’s September 16 release reports that the Board voted 7-1-1 on September 15 for an immediate pause on certain legislative data center and substation applications during Phase 2, with a separate 7-1-1 grid-reliability exception. It reports grandfathered administrative cases are unaffected. On October 20 a formal resolution with a proposed 12-month per-application limit was deferred to November 17, according to October 21 reporting; this does not establish repeal of the earlier action. Current legal effect and scope remain qualified pending primary confirmation. The earlier record attributes the separate exception vote opposition to Supervisor Briskman and reports that the Board was to receive legal analysis on October 6 concerning grandfathered cases without vested rights.
- **Outcome:** Loudoun County reported an immediate pause on Board consideration of certain legislative data center and substation applications during its Phase 2 review, subject to applicable deadlines and a grid-reliability exception. A later proposed formal resolution was deferred.

### Virginia Beach

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** 2026-08-18, Virginia Beach City Council, unanimous vote.
- **Date field:** `2026-08-18` (exact)
- **Duration:** 12 months from adoption, or until City Council takes final action on an ordinance regulating data centers, whichever occurs first (to approximately 2027-08-18).
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `va-virginia-beach-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Resolution adopted by Virginia Beach City Council on August 18, 2026, pausing the issuance of permits related to any new data center for 12 months or until Council takes final action on an ordinance regulating data centers, whichever occurs first; follows planning staff's finding that data centers are currently classified, by default, as wholesaling/warehousing/storage/distribution uses permitted by right in industrial districts.
- **What prompted it:** City zoning ordinance does not specifically define or regulate data centers; concerns raised over resource consumption (water, electricity), noise, and land-use compatibility, following an informal June 2026 Council statement opposing large-scale/hyperscale data centers.
- **Affected projects:** No large-scale storage/computing data center currently operates in Virginia Beach; existing subsea-cable landing and carrier-neutral colocation facilities (e.g., Globalinx) are not affected.
- **Status notes:** Active as of 2026-09-23. Virginia Beach City Council unanimously adopted a 12-month moratorium on new data center permits on August 18, 2026, the same night Chesapeake City Council closed its by-right loophole. The moratorium does not affect existing facilities such as Globalinx's subsea-cable colocation operations, and is intended to apply to future larger-scale and hyperscale data center proposals while the city studies zoning definitions, setbacks, and noise standards. No repeal, extension, or replacement ordinance was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
- **Outcome:** Virginia Beach City Council unanimously adopted a 12-month moratorium on new data center permits while it develops zoning definitions and regulations for the industry.

### HB1515 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `va-hb1515-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Del. Irene Shin; D
- **Status:** Presented, ordered printed and referred to House Rules 2026-01-23; subcommittee recommended continuing to 2027 (Voice Vote) 2026-02-02; Continued to 2027 in Rules Committee (Voice Vote) 2026-02-06.
- **Provisions:** Introduced HB1515 would prohibit local final approval of a rezoning, special exception, special use permit, site plan, or plan of development for siting a new data center until the earlier of fulfillment of all pending data-center-customer requests for interconnection to electric utility distribution service or 2028-07-01. Data center is defined by reference to § 58.1-3506(A)(43).

### HB153 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `va-hb153-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Del. Joshua E. Thomas; D
- **Status:** Passed House 2026-01-29 (90-Y 7-N); incorporates HB511 (McAuliff) 2026-01-23; passed Senate with substitute 2026-03-11 (26-Y 14-N); conference report agreed to by House and Senate 2026-03-14; enrolled 2026-03-30; Enacted, Chapter 567, approved by Governor 2026-04-13, effective 2026-07-01.
- **Provisions:** Published chapter/code site-assessment framework requires an applicant's sound assessment before specified local approvals for a new facility reasonably anticipated to require at least 100 MW of retail utility power. Sound impacts concern homes and schools within 500 feet of the facility property boundary; other resource assessments are optional, and utility substation/voltage information is also required subject to stated qualifications. The framework preserves the existing-approval/expansion exception; its phrase “does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more” is not converted into a definitive boundary here. The chapter labels the provision 15.2-2209.4; the observed code publishes it as 15.2-2209.5. Later force is not independently confirmed.
- **Mechanism / scope:** permitting_restriction; local_government
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-07-01
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20261/HB153>)

### HB155 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `va-hb155-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Del. Joshua E. Thomas; D
- **Status:** Prefiled 2026-01-06; referred to House Labor and Commerce; subcommittee recommended laying on the table (9-Y 0-N) 2026-02-10; left in Labor and Commerce 2026-02-18; official retained page labels the bill failed.
- **Provisions:** Introduced HB155 would require an SCC certificate before operating a facility, or facilities effectively operating together at the Commission's discretion, with electricity demand or contracted capacity exceeding 25 MW and not operating before 2026-07-01. Certification follows applicable notice and hearing and requires specified findings on rates, reliability, utility compliance, clean-energy policy and public interest; review includes grid capacity, environmental and public-health impacts and cross-subsidy. An adequate showing of specified contracts or other measures designed to offset system peak demand creates presumptions on certain findings, not an exemption from the certificate requirement.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20261/HB155>)

### HB1601 (2025)

- **Policy ID:** `va-hb1601-2025`
- **Sponsor / party:** Del. Joshua E. Thomas; D
- **Status:** Passed House 2025-01-23 (57-Y 40-N); passed Senate with substitute 2025-02-12; conference report agreed to by Senate 2025-02-21 and House 2025-02-22; enrolled 2025-03-07; House rejected Governor's recommended amendments 2025-04-02 (11-Y 85-N); vetoed by Governor 2025-05-02. The April2 return followed rejection of recommended amendments during the2025 reconvened session. ArticleVsection6(c)(iii) makes the Governor’s May2veto of a returned bill final: that veto stands and the bill does not become law; this is distinct from the ordinary override procedure.
- **Provisions:** Enrolled HB1601 would require a locality, before approval of specified zoning applications for a new high energy use facility, to require the applicant to assess its sound profile on residential units and schools within 500 feet of the property boundary, to the extent practicable and within the statutory timeline. A facility qualifies when the applicant reasonably anticipates at application that it will require 100 MW or more of retail utility power. The locality may require specified resource assessments on the site or immediately contiguous land, and must require qualified utility substation and transmission information. The existing-approval expansion or modification exception states that the expansion 'does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more'; its numeric boundary is unresolved. Existing local zoning authority is preserved. The enrolled print has blank chapter and approval fields; the retained returned-bill sequence and ArticleVsection6(c)(iii) establish the final May2veto rather than an operative statute. The expansion-boundary wording remains an explicit ambiguity in the failed enrolled proposal, not a current legal requirement.
- **Mechanism / scope:** reporting_disclosure; statewide
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20251/HB1601>)

### HB503 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `va-hb503-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Del. John Chilton McAuliff; D
- **Status:** Prefiled 2026-01-12; referred to House Labor and Commerce; subcommittee recommended continuing to 2027 (Voice Vote) 2026-02-10; Continued to 2027 in Labor and Commerce (Voice Vote) 2026-02-12.
- **Provisions:** Introduced HB503 would bar inclusion in SCC-approved rates or charges under § 56-585.1 or § 56-585.8 of Phase I or Phase II utility costs, including increased fuel, generation and transmission costs, that are substantially related to electric service to data center customers and would not have been incurred but for their demand, unless the rates or charges are designed to recover, or substantially recover, those costs solely from data center customers. For this provision, a data center customer is a data center under § 58.1-3506(A)(43) with peak demand of 100 MW or greater.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** proposed

### SB553 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `va-sb553-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Kannan Srinivasan; D
- **Status:** Passed Senate 2026-02-09 (25-Y 15-N); passed House with substitute 2026-03-02 (81-Y 18-N); conference report agreed to 2026-03-14; enrolled 2026-03-30; Enacted, Chapter 896, approved by Governor 2026-04-13, effective 2027-01-01.
- **Provisions:** Published water-reporting act requires covered registered offsite suppliers to report potable and reclaimed water separately for qualifying air-permitted data centers. Other use categories are required to the extent available without utility billing-system modifications; quarterly volumes may substitute where monthly data are unavailable. The act expressly becomes effective 2027-01-01; enactment does not establish that it was already operative at the observation date.

### SB94 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `va-sb94-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Danica A. Roem; D
- **Status:** Incorporates SB130 (Ebbin) 2026-02-03; passed Senate 2026-02-12 (21-Y 18-N 1-A); passed House with substitute 2026-02-25 (80-Y 14-N); conference report agreed to 2026-03-14; enrolled 2026-03-30; Enacted, Chapter 568, approved by Governor 2026-04-13, effective 2026-07-01.
- **Provisions:** Observed code site-assessment framework requires an applicant's sound assessment before specified local approvals for a new facility reasonably anticipated to require at least 100 MW of retail utility power. Sound impacts concern homes and schools within 500 feet of the facility property boundary; other resource assessments are optional, and utility substation/voltage information is also required subject to stated qualifications. The framework preserves the existing-approval/expansion exception; its phrase “does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more” is not converted into a definitive boundary here. The observed code publishes the framework as 15.2-2209.5 and cites chapters 567 and 568. Direct comparison confirms that all seven subsections A-G of the retained Chapter 568 data-center text match the retained code text after whitespace normalization, although the chapter prints 15.2-2209.4 and the code publishes 15.2-2209.5. A separate enactment, Chapter 1075 (HB888, approved April22,2026), also adds 15.2-2209.4 for parking, which the observed code publishes at that number. This documents the same-number conflict and the observed allocation; formal editorial renumbering authority and later legal changes/current force have not been independently established.
- **Mechanism / scope:** permitting_restriction; local_government
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-07-01
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://lis.virginia.gov/bill-details/20261/SB94>)
